sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145084
Court No. - 36
Case :- Writ - A No. - 10981 of 2023

Petitioner :- Malkhan Singh
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 4 Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Kamal Kumar Kesherwani
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Bipin Bihari Pandey
Hon'ble Manjive Shukla,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Standing Counsel appearing for Respondents No. 1 and 2 as well as Ms. Shruti Malviya, learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.3.
2.
The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner was engaged as Shiksha Mitra in Primary School Aruho, Block Haseran, District Kannauj on 10.07.2004.

Petitioner continued to work in the capacity of Shiksha Mitra but in the year 2018 a criminal case was lodged against the petitioner bearing Case Crime No. 472 of 2018 under Sections 420, 342, 376, 120-B, 506 I.P.C.
3. Petitioner in connection to aforesaid criminal case was arrested and sent to judicial custody.
Later on the petitioner has been released on bail on 22.08.2019.
4. Petitioner after his release on bail submitted representation before the Respondent No.3 and thereby requested that he may be allowed to work as Shiksha Mitra.

sentences.text: Since respondents did not allow the petitioner to work on the post of Shiksha Mitra then petitioner filed Writ-A No. 11453 of 2022 and the said writ petition was finally disposed of vide order dated 05.08.2022.

Operative portion of the order dated 05.08.2022 is extracted as under :-
"In the facts and circumstances of the case, without entering into the merits and with the consent of the parties, direction is issued to the respondent no.3 District Basic Education Officer, Kannauj to decide the representation/claim of the petitioner dated 20.6.2022 (Annexure-8 to the writ petition) by reasoned and speaking order in accordance with law expeditiously, preferably within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
With the above direction, the writ petition stands finally disposed of."

6. In compliance of the aforesaid order dated 05.08.2022 passed in Writ-A No. 11453 of 2022 District Basic Education Officer, Kannauj has passed order on 13.09.2022 which is impugned in the present writ petition.

District Basic Education Officer, Kannauj in his order dated 13.09.2022 has recorded a finding that the petitioner was sent to judicial custody in the year 2018 and since then he was not working as Shiksha Mitra and therefore, his case for renewal as Shiksha Mitra was not considered and further since about five years have lapsed, there is no occasion to allow him to work as Shiksha Mitra.

7. Learned counsel for the petitioner has vehemently argued that under the Government Order dated 15.06.2022 petitioner has a right to get his engagement as Shiksha Mitra renewed and the procedure prescribed under the Government Order dated 15.06.2022 provides that renewal of all the Shiksha Mitra will be automatic and further if there is any adverse material in respect of the work and conduct of a Shiksha Mitra then the Gram Shiksha Samiti by 31st of May of the concerned year shall submit a comprehensive report to District Basic Education Officer and thereafter the District Basic Education Officer shall place the entire material before the District Level Committee headed by District Magistrate and after the approval of the District Magistrate, the case for renewal of Shiksha Mitra shall be rejected.
8.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that in the present case it was incumbent upon the respondents to pass order of renewal of the engagement of the Shiksha Mitra of the petitioner only in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the Government Order dated 15.06.2022 whereas District Basic Education Officer on his own has passed the impugned order dated 13.09.2022 wherein he has said that the petitioner cannot be allowed to join on his post as Shiksha Mitra.
9. I have considered the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the petitioner and I have also heard Ms. Shruti Malviya, learned counsel appearing for Respondent No.3.

10. I find that once the petitioner was implicated in a criminal case and he was sent to judicial custody then if work and conduct of the petitioner was such that his engagement as Shiksha Mitra could not have been renewed then the concerned Gram Shiksha Samiti ought to have submitted a Malkhan Singh vs State Of U.P. And 4 Others on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159352110/
2 report through District Basic Education Officer and thereafter the matter ought to have been placed before the District Level Committee headed by the District Magistrate and only after the approval of the District Magistrate the case for renewal of the term of petitioner as Shiksha Mitra could have been rejected.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said exercise has not been done in the case of the petitioner at all.

11. Since the procedure prescribed under the Government Order dated 15.06.2022 has not been followed which is apparent from a bare reading of the impugned order dated 13.09.2022, therefore,
the impugned order cannot sustain in the eyes of law.
12. In view of the aforesaid reasons this writ petition is allowed.

Impugned order dated 13.09.2022 is quashed and matter is remanded to District Basic Education Officer, Kannauj for fresh decision in the matter after following due procedure prescribed under the Government Order dated 15.06.2022.
The aforesaid exercise shall be completed expeditiously preferably, within a period of two months from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
